Disney beats fourth-quarter estimates, targets $3 billion in savings through cost-cutting efforts

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and unveiled it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal 2029.
  • Recent findings suggest that those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs announced in recent months, Disney's chief financial officer, Hugh Johnston, told CNBC.
  • Future cost-saving measures will include reductions in administrative and other general expenses, Johnston mentioned, while adding, "We do expect more layoffs.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and unveiled it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal 2029.

Recent findings suggest that those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs announced in recent months, Disney's chief financial officer, Hugh Johnston, told CNBC. The most recent round, which seeks to reduce costs by up to 20%, was reported earlier this month.

Future cost-saving measures will include reductions in administrative and other general expenses, Johnston mentioned, while adding, "We do expect more layoffs.".

Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro told investors on the company's earnings call that the job cuts are "not easy.".

In a recent development, "They affect people who care deeply about Disney and have contributed so much to this tech giant," he noted. "At the same time, these steps are crucial if we want to be a company that moves faster, adapts to a rapidly changing environment, and keeps investing in the content and technology that will drive our growth.".

The cuts will help Disney fund its $26 billion in projected content spend for fiscal 2027, a 9% increase from fiscal 2026.

The entertainment giant is also forecasting double-digit growth in earnings per share in the next fiscal year, as well as segment operating income growth of around 8%.

Disney noted that the majority of that growth will be concentrated in the first half of the year due to the theatrical debut of "Avengers: Doomsday" and a boost from the Super Bowl, which will air on Disney's ESPN and ABC networks.

"The growth is really going to come in the first half of this year," Johnston remarked. "That's the opposite of what we saw in '26, where the growth was backloaded.".

Sources indicate that the company will also increase its annual dividend to $2 a share, a 33% increase from the previously declared dividend. It will be payable in two installments of $1 per share, one in January and one in July.

Sources indicate that here's how Disney performed in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Oct. 3, compared with what Wall Street expected, according to LSEG:.

Disney reported net income for the fiscal fourth quarter of $2.61 billion, or $1.51 per share, compared with $1.31 billion, or 73 cents per share, during the same period the year prior.

Adjusting for one-time items, including severance and other restructuring charges as well as the value of intangible assets, Disney reported earnings per share of $1.77.

The company's revenue for the quarter was 16% higher year over year, and results were once again lifted by its parks and streaming divisions.

Disney's experiences segment, which includes its theme parks and cruises, reported nearly $10.11 billion in revenue, up 15% year over year. Operating income for the unit increased 20% to $2.25 billion.

The division is already a top performer for the manufacturer, but it benefited in the fiscal fourth quarter because of an extra calendar week compared with the previous fiscal year.

While international attendance continues to lag at Disney's domestic parks, it is being offset by domestic attendance, especially at the Walt Disney World resort in Orlando, Florida, Johnston said.

Industry observers note that growth at Disneyland Paris was driven by recent investments including an expansion area called World of Frozen. Attendance at the Hong Kong and Shanghai parks remained soft because of broad economic challenges in those regions, according to Disney.

Still, D'Amaro said he believes the growth in parks will be sustainable through next year, especially with fresh additions, including the "Monsters, Inc."-themed land "Monstropolis" opening at Walt Disney World in 2027.

"Q1 forward resort bookings at Walt Disney World are pacing up compared to the prior year," he stated. "And latest capacity and new experiences will start coming online in 2027. We keep investing to make the experience fresh, and what we see is that drives repeat visits.".

In a recent development, the company expects operating income for the experiences segment to grow in the high-single digits in fiscal 2027. Growth is expected to be front-loaded as the company laps the launch of the Disney Adventure cruise ship, which set sail in March.

According to recent reports, over at its entertainment division, Disney saw revenue increase 17% to $11.89 billion. Operating income nearly doubled to $1.33 billion.

Revenue from streaming, specifically, rose 19% to $6.1 billion, Disney remarked.

Recent findings suggest that the segment benefited from the extra week on the fiscal calendar as well as from growth in subscription and affiliate fees. Additionally, the tech giant saw higher theatrical distribution revenue from titles like "Toy Story 5.".

Disney remarked Tuesday it expects operating income for the entertainment division to grow in the high-single digits in the coming fiscal year.

The firm's sports division saw revenue increase 16% in the fiscal fourth quarter, reaching $4.61 billion. Operating income for the segment surged more than 50% to $1.39 billion.

Subscription and affiliate fees fueled this growth alongside an increase in advertising revenue.

According to recent reports, the firm expects its sports division's operating income to grow by double digits in fiscal 2027. It noted that the fiscal first quarter of the year will see some declines because of the timing of College Football Playoff games and the Fresh Year's window. However, the fiscal second quarter will benefit from the college championship as well as the broadcast of Super Bowl 61.

Disney's outlook for overall and segment results for fiscal 2027 excludes the impact of a 53rd week in fiscal 2026.

Sources indicate that D'Amaro has made advancing technology a pillar of the organization's growth strategy. In September, Disney hired Karandeep Anand in the newly created position of chief technology officer.

Industry observers note that "Technology is central to how we connect fans to more of Disney and drive returns on our investment," D'Amaro said on the earnings call. "[Anand has] been energized by how much opportunity he sees to move faster and go further in product and technology. Done right, that means serving our fans even better, working more efficiently and being more innovative across every one of our businesses.".

Disney confirmed a partnership with Adobe earlier this month to develop generative artificial intelligence models.

D'Amaro told investors that the team is exploring ways to use AI to make booking trips to Disney parks easier.

It has been revealed that "There's actually a vacation planning tool that's in beta right now at Walt Disney World. We built that with our partners at Google, and I've had a chance to experiment with it myself," he noted. "It'll be incredibly helpful for our guests who are booking trips. With these AI features, it can feel like you've got someone sitting right by your side, like a personal concierge, that aims and responds to the way that you want to actually book your trip to Walt Disney World.".

According to recent reports, the entertainment organization has also expanded its short-form content, adding a vertical video channel within the Disney+ mobile app. The company had previously unveiled a partnership with TikTok to bring creator content to the streaming app.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When India's world chess champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, faced reporters at the pre-tournament press conference in Geneva on Sunday, there was no sign of the youthful, carefree energy one might expect from a 20-year-old.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When India's world chess champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, faced reporters at the pre-tournament press conference in Geneva on Sunday, there was no sign of the youthful, carefree energy one might expect from a 20-year-old.

"I don't think I'm here to defend anything—I'm here to win it all over again," he remarked.

Starting November 24, Gukesh will be facing challenger Jakhovir Sindarov of Uzbekistan for a purse of $2.5 million (€2.3m) in the World Chess Championship.

Gukesh captured the title in 2024, making him the youngest-ever world champion at just 18. Since then, however, things have not as gone well for the player known for his exceptional calculation skills and a penchant for risky moves. He presently languishes in 26th place in the FIDE world rankings.

Sindarov, who has climbed to number four in the world, told reporters that he only began training "seriously" last year and has learned a lot from observing the reigning world champion.

"He has a very good strength in typical positions, his calculation is very good, and Gukesh can fight until the end," Sindarov said.

Former world champion Viswanathan Anand, who was also one of the world's best players as a teenager, is not completely surprised by Gukesh's lack of form over the past two years.

According to recent reports, "He became the world champion (very young). So suddenly the responsibility is shifted onto you and even expectations," Anand told DW.

"Clearly he has deficiencies in his chess as is normal for someone who's 20, he's not had time to experience a lot.".

By the time he became India's first world champion, Anand was 37 – ancient by the age-standards of today's top players.

"With powerful chess software and global connectivity, it is easier for young players today to reach the top level," Jan Gustafsson, coach of Germany's national chess team, told DW.

"Online chess provides many more learning opportunities for talented players," added Gustafsson, who sees the recent movement at the top of the rankings as a "generational shift.".

While Norway's Magnus Carlsen, long considered the greatest player of all time, remains number one in the world rankings, he rarely plays classical chess anymore and gave up his world championship title after declining to defend it in 2023.

Sources indicate that now, young players—particularly from Asia—are pushing to the forefront. Alongside Gukesh and Sindarov, players such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa from India and Nodirbek Abdusattorov of Uzbekistan—an emerging chess powerhouse—are considered contenders to win a world championship in the not-too-distant future.

"Broad social acceptance and state support ensure that children can focus on chess at a very early stage," Gustafsson said.

Another contender is Germany's Vincent Keymer, who at 22 is number nine in the world and well established among the world's elite. Most recently, Keymer and his teammates won a bronze medal at the World Team Championship, often referred to as the "Chess Olympiad.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that on Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that the 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus.
  • Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station debuted into orbit.

Recent findings suggest that the 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket. Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit.

Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian tech giant to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

According to recent reports, today, the International Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze.

It has been revealed that as of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece.

And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station.

Recent findings suggest that zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet.

In a recent development, NASA paid $220 million for Zarya's construction at the Krunichev State Research and Production Space Center in Moscow, with work beginning in 1994 and ending in 1998. The module is a central hub based on the success of Russia's Salyut space station designs, with two solar arrays for power and 16 external tanks to store propellant.

While NASA's space shuttle Endeavour was the first to meet Zarya (and attach NASA's core Unity connecting module to it), it wasn't until Russia'z Zvezda service rolled out in 2000 and docked with Zarya's aft that the fledgling space station was large enough to accomodate its first three-person crew, Expedition 1.

In a recent development, over the last 28 years, giant backbone-like metal trusses, solar wings and many other modules (built by Russia, NASA, Europe, Canada and Japan) have greatly expanded the living area of the station. Many ISS components could not be tested with one another on the ground, meaning the first time they were attached was in space during construction.

The result is a feat of space construction that has only recently seen a rival as China works to expand its own Tiangong space station.

Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that vitamin C may do more than support everyday health.
  • Industry observers note that exposure to nitrates and nitrites has increased in North American diets over the past several decades.
  • It has been revealed that one of these reactions, called nitrosation, can produce substances that researchers suspect may contribute to cancer development.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that vitamin C may do more than support everyday health. Newly introduced research from the University of Waterloo suggests that it could also help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming during digestion. Using mathematical modeling, scientists investigated how vitamin C influences chemical reactions in the digestive system that have been linked to cancer risk.

Industry observers note that exposure to nitrates and nitrites has increased in North American diets over the past several decades. These compounds are found in cured meats such as bacon and salami, as well as in fruits and vegetables grown in soil or water affected by pollution. Although nitrates and nitrites contribute to important functions in the brain and cardiovascular system, they can also participate in potentially harmful reactions once they reach the stomach.

It has been revealed that one of these reactions, called nitrosation, can produce substances that researchers suspect may contribute to cancer development. Understanding what causes these chemicals to form, and what might prevent their formation, has been a longstanding challenge.

Why Vitamin C Could Change the Cancer Risk Equation.

In a recent development, "Since at least the 90s, researchers have been studying the link between cancer and these compounds, with conflicting results," noted Dr. Gordon McNicol, a post-doctoral researcher in applied mathematics and the first author of the study. "Our work suggests that the presence of dietary Vitamin C may help explain these inconsistencies.".

Sources indicate that to investigate this possibility, the researchers developed a mathematical model that simulates how nitrates and nitrites travel through the body and undergo chemical changes. The model incorporated several interconnected systems, including the salivary glands, stomach, small intestine, and plasma, the liquid portion of blood.

Their simulations revealed that vitamin C consumed alongside nitrates and nitrites may interfere with the formation of potentially harmful compounds. This could help explain why foods containing nitrates do not necessarily carry the same risks.

Sources indicate that for example, leafy vegetables such as spinach naturally contain both nitrates and vitamin C. According to the model, the presence of vitamin C could limit the chemical reactions associated with cancer risk, potentially helping explain the protective effects suggested by some dietary research.

Could Taking Vitamin C After Meals Help?

The researchers also explored whether vitamin C supplements might offer similar benefits when taken after eating.

In a recent development, their findings suggest that taking vitamin C after each meal could moderately reduce the formation of nitrosation products associated with cancer risk. This effect could be particularly relevant when consuming foods containing nitrates and nitrites, including processed meats such as bacon and salami.

Recent findings suggest that however, the results come from mathematical simulations rather than clinical trials. Although the model predicts that vitamin C can reduce the production of potentially harmful chemicals, further research is needed to determine whether this translates into a measurable reduction in cancer risk in humans.

Latest Clues for Future Cancer Prevention Research.

It has been revealed that the researchers believe their model could help scientists better understand the complicated relationship between diet, digestive chemistry, and cancer risk. It may also provide guidance for future experiments examining how nutritional choices influence the formation of potentially harmful compounds.

"This work provides a mechanistic roadmap for future clinical and laboratory studies by identifying the key interacting drivers of these potentially harmful chemical reactions, including nitrite exposure, antioxidant intake, meal timing, gastric conditions and oral microbiome activity," remarked Dr. Anita Layton, professor of applied mathematics and Canada 150 researcher chair. "This model can help researchers design more targeted experiments and interventions, focusing on when and in whom nitrosation is most likely to occur.".

By identifying how factors such as vitamin C intake, meal timing, stomach conditions, and bacteria in the mouth interact, the model could help researchers develop more precise strategies for studying and potentially reducing cancer-related chemical reactions during digestion.

The study, "Vitamin C as a nitrosation inhibitor: A modelling study across dietary patterns and water quality," was published in the Journal of Theoretical Biology.

Two goals in 15 games - what's going on with Gyokeres?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (961 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Viktor Gyokeres has scored twice in all competitions this season.
  • A Premier League trophy and 21 goals in his debut season - on paper things have worked out perfectly for Viktor Gyokeres since his Â£64m transfer to Arsenal.
  • But, even with those achievements, it has been a tough start to the current campaign for the 28-year-old striker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Viktor Gyokeres has scored twice in all competitions this season.

A Premier League trophy and 21 goals in his debut season - on paper things have worked out perfectly for Viktor Gyokeres since his Â£64m transfer to Arsenal.

But, even with those achievements, it has been a tough start to the current campaign for the 28-year-old striker.

The Swede has started just one Premier League game this season and is yet to score in his eight league appearances.

He has started three games in the Champions League, two in the Carabao Cup, and has scored just twice in 15 games in all competitions. Not the numbers he would have hoped for after last season's glory.

It is not just this season that has seen Gyokeres suitability questioned for Arsenal though.

Even though he scored more than 20 goals in his first season in all competitions as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait for a title, his all-round game had its critics.

It has been near enough a straight battle for the number nine role between Kai Havertz and Gyokeres since the Swedish international signed.

And Gyokeres was thrust into leading the line for Arsenal quicker and more frequently than planned after injury kept Havertz out for long periods last season.

Although the Swede may be the more natural finisher, Havertz's all-round play is considered superior with the German also one of Arteta's most trusted players for major games.

Gyokeres, a "win-now signing", was bought for his ability to find the net but also for how he could open up spaces for his team-mates, something they have praised him for.

But playing with his back to goal and linking up play is not natural to Gyokeres and his failure to hold up the ball or win duels with centre-backs has led to fan frustration.

Arteta has spoken about how the striker has been working on improving his hold-up play and connections, and there were hints of it in the Champions League win over Slavia Prague where Gyokeres assisted the opener and scored the winner in arguably his best game of the season.

Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious'.

A substantial reason that Gyokeres is not starting games is that Havertz is fit.

Last season, Havertz suffered with knee and hamstring issues which meant Gyokeres was the only option Arteta had.

Had Havertz been fit, he would have played a lot more and the fact that he started the Champions League final and the key match away at Manchester City in last season's title race back this up.

This season Gyokeres has just six starts and Arteta says that his gametime and situation is similar to other members in the squad.

"We have rotated the team a lot and used the competitions as well to give minutes to players and exposure because they are all starters in my opinion," Arteta said.

"Viktor's case is one of many that they have been in the same situation where they play more in the Premier League or more in the Champions League which is not bad, eh?".

Arteta is open with his players about their standing in the squad and said that Gyokeres has not approached him directly about a lack of minutes.

"We have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing and to gather information about the way we are feeling and so far it has been very positive with Viktor and the rest of the team," he remarked.

The signing of Gyokeres is an interesting one in its own right.

The Arsenal recruitment team had done a lot of due diligence on signing, now Manchester United forward, Benjamin Sesko.

It is understood work on that deal had been done but a change of direction to sign Gyokeres happened after Andrea Berta became Arsenal sporting director.

Some around Arsenal have always thought that Gyokeres is not the usual forward that the Gunners would go for and his predicament of a lack of game time was always likely to happen, even if he did play a big part in them ending their trophy drought.

Gyokeres ended last season with 14 league goals but those strikes actually only won Arsenal two points on their way to winning the league.

That is because, although his penalty in the 1-0 win at Everton was the only goal of the game, Arsenal would have come away with a draw, so that strike factually only accounted for two points and not three.

But Gyokeres did put the Gunners ahead five times last season in the league which shows that, among the frustrating performances, he had plenty of impact.

Max Dowman stole the show with his goal in the 2-0 home win over Everton, when he became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, but it was Gyokeres' goal in the 89th-minute which put Arsenal ahead and although it did not lead to a point score on its own, it set them on the way.

Gyokeres also scored in the 4-1 north London derby win, putting Arsenal ahead when Kolo Muani had equalised after Eberechi Eze's opener.

It is unlikely that Gyokeres will be sold in January as he continues to get games in the Champions League and is a senior player who can score goals in big moments.

But if his lack of minutes in the league continue, Gyokeres, who is a driven and ambitious individual, will not want to be the player who is left out of the starting XI in the long term.

Additional reporting Chris Collinson, BBC Sport Football data analyst and Sami Mokbel senior football correspondent.

📅 03 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (765 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNN ↗ Open Full Page

Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the New York Times

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (765 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some VIP Twitter customers woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by Elon Musk.
  • Twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile consumers at risk of impersonation — on April 1.
  • But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Latest York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some VIP Twitter customers woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by Elon Musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

Twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile consumers at risk of impersonation — on April 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Latest York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

William Shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue Twitter checkmark. Elon Musk says too bad.

After an account that often engages with Musk posted a meme this weekend about the Times declining to pay for verification, Musk responded in a tweet saying, “Oh ok, we’ll take it off then.” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda.”.

The weekend moves are just the latest example of Twitter creating confusion and whiplash for owners over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

Although the Newly introduced York Times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post.) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not plan to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sources indicate that in a separate puzzling move, Twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on Monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which Musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from people verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

In early November, Twitter launched the option for people paying for its Twitter Blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was promptly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual people would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent owners such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

By muddying the reason accounts are verified, the new label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile users. Experts in inauthentic behavior have also noted it’s not clear that reserving verification for paid users will reduce the number of bots on the site, an concern Musk has raised on and off over the past year.

Musk, for his part, has previously presented changes to Twitter’s verification system as a way of “treating everyone equally.”.

It has been revealed that “There shouldn’t be a different standard for celebrities,” he stated in a tweet last week. The paid feature could also drive revenue, which could help Musk, who is on the hook for significant debt after buying Twitter for $44 billion.

Musk last week also mentioned that starting on April 15, only verified accounts would be recommended in users’ “For You” feeds alongside the accounts they follow.

–CNN’s Oliver Darcy contributed to this report.

Tech Report: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that emerging research suggests that biological sex and genetics may play a major role in how neurological disorders develop, progress, and respond to treatment.
  • Researchers are increasingly finding that certain neurological conditions can behave differently depending on a person's biological sex and genetic makeup.
  • Two of the latest studies highlight how menopause and inherited genetic factors may influence Alzheimer's vulnerability and treatment responses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that emerging research suggests that biological sex and genetics may play a major role in how neurological disorders develop, progress, and respond to treatment. The findings, which will be presented at Neuroscience 2026, reveal vital differences that could help researchers develop more personalized approaches to treating complex brain conditions. Neuroscience 2026 is the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience and the world's largest source of emerging news about brain science and health.

Researchers are increasingly finding that certain neurological conditions can behave differently depending on a person's biological sex and genetic makeup. Understanding these differences could lead to treatments better suited to each individual's biology. Two conditions receiving particular attention are Alzheimer's disease (AD), an incurable disorder that progressively damages memory and other brain functions, and fibromyalgia, a chronic illness marked by persistent pain and fatigue that affects 2-4% of the global population. According to the World Health Organization, Alzheimer's affects between 35 and 40 million people worldwide.

Menopause, Genetics, and Alzheimer's Disease.

Two of the latest studies highlight how menopause and inherited genetic factors may influence Alzheimer's vulnerability and treatment responses.

It has been revealed that one investigation found that people carrying genetic risk factors for Alzheimer's responded differently to menopause hormone therapy (MHT) compared with those without the same genetic risks. The effects also varied according to the particular combination of hormones used. These findings suggest that both genetic background and hormone therapy formulation deserve consideration when evaluating treatment options. (Mateja Perović, University of Toronto).

Sources indicate that A separate study examined rodents undergoing menopause that also carried genetic risk factors for Alzheimer's. Researchers observed that brain circuits responsible for memory became particularly vulnerable, providing evidence that menopause may represent an notable period of increased susceptibility for women who are genetically predisposed to the disease. (Stephanie M. Perez, University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio).

Sex Differences in Chronic Pain and Brain Inflammation.

The other two studies explored how biological sex influences pain sensitivity, immune activity, and the effects of inflammation on the brain.

In a mouse model of fibromyalgia, females continued to show heightened sensitivity to touch and stronger immune system activation compared with males. The findings suggest that the biological processes contributing to chronic pain may differ between sexes, potentially making treatments tailored to these differences more effective. (Yasmin Sahlloul, University of Cincinnati).

According to recent reports, another investigation uncovered differences in how prolonged intestinal inflammation influences the brain. Using a mouse model, researchers found that chronic gut inflammation affected brain function and Alzheimer's related disease changes differently in males and females. The results provide additional evidence that biological sex may influence the relationship between inflammation and neurological disease. (Nurcan Kilic, University of North Dakota).

Toward More Personalized Treatments for Brain Disorders.

According to recent reports, together, the four studies underscore the importance of examining sex and genetic differences when investigating neurological conditions. By identifying biological factors that influence disease progression and treatment responses, researchers hope to move toward more precise therapies for Alzheimer's, fibromyalgia, and other difficult-to-treat brain disorders.

"These four studies illustrate the fascinating discoveries that can be made when focusing on female-specific biology or possible sex differences in AD-related symptoms and risk factors," remarked Liisa Galea, PhD, Treliving Family Chair in Women's Mental Health at Centre for Addiction and Mental Health and moderator of the press conference. "The research presented at Neuroscience 2026 helps us pinpoint the specific differences that may help us develop more targeted treatment using precision approaches, even for some of our most complex brain disorders.".

Fiona first rose to fame when she was born premature at Cincinnati Zoo in 2017.

Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.

Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 2017, died on Thursday after swallowing a woollen hat that had slipped into her enclosure.

The Ohio side will now raise a banner depicting the nine-year-old semi-aquatic mammal in their post-season MLS Cup encounter with Nashville, who won the Supporters' Shield for being the highest-placed team in the league campaign.

Cincinnati mentioned Fiona was a "beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world".

The tifo will be produced by fan group The Forge Cincy, who painted the display on Sunday in a garage next to Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.

The club will also make a donation in Fiona's memory for every fan in attendance to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden.

Fan group The Forge Cincy had previously spent two weeks creating a tifo for their "Hell is Real" October derby match against Ohio rivals Columbus.

Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo states.

Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo.

Cincinnati's Nick Hagglund, who hails from the city and is in his eighth season with the team, previously paid tribute to Fiona after scoring in his side's 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day of her death.

The defender yelled "that's for Fiona", mimicking the ears on top of her head, in a celebration video, external on the club's Instagram.

Later, on his Instagram account, external, Hagglund posted, "This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.

"Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call.".

Cincinnati's tifo is one of a number of tributes paid to the hippo, with Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins wearing a Fiona sweater, external prior to his American football franchise's defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday.

Meanwhile handlers of the blue hippo balloon at Latest York's annual Macy's Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.

At birth, Fiona weighed 13kg (29lb), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species, and she previously inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

From premature baby to social media star - famed Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies.

Fiona swallowed the woollen hat around 10 days prior to her death, with the item getting into her enclosure by accident after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," noted zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.

Hippos normally live up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.

Nashville finished top of the MLS Eastern Conference, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati.

However, having beaten Orlando in a one-off wildcard round, Cincinnati defeated Nashville 1-0 in the opening match of their best-of-three round one series.

Should Cincinnati win on Saturday they will progress to a one-off conference semi-final with either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC, with a conference final prior to the season-ending MLS Cup final.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX debuted a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.

Sources indicate that A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317.

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.

SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit.

Recent findings suggest that USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world.

NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions.

USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has rolled out for the Space Force so far in November.

The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which at the moment consists of more than 11,000 satellites.

The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025, for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out. SpaceX looks to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on a Sunday morning in April, minutes from the US Capitol and down a stretch of Washington, DC’s Pennsylvania Avenue, a wall of black SUVs lined up alongside yellow police tape. Men in military gear held long guns and guarded the entrance to a mirrored window and door.

This is Christ Church DC, a place of worship that appeared on Capitol Hill a year ago.

That Sunday, high-ranking government officials, including Homeland Security's intelligence chief, America’s top international health diplomat, and the government’s international finance chief, had gathered to hear a sermon. “It gives a whole fresh meaning to worshipping in the presence of your enemies,” quipped the pastor, referencing the church’s location. “We’ve asked the government to fix us, and we’re more enslaved than ever.”.

Christ Church DC arrived after Pete Hegseth, who regularly attends worship with his family, was confirmed as US secretary of defense.

The church is part of Pastor Doug Wilson’s network, known as the CREC—the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches—which is headquartered in Moscow, Idaho. Wilson’s long-held goal is to turn America into a theocracy, where all its institutions are molded in accordance with biblical law, executions are made public, non-Christians are barred from holding office, and women submit to their husbands instead of voting.

According to recent reports, WIRED has identified around a dozen government officials who have attended services at Christ Church DC at least once since it opened a year ago. Other officials who have attended include a top-ranking Pentagon adviser, a former senior Marine Corps pilot who now oversees personnel affairs in the Navy, and a federal immigration judge with a history of attracting complaints of volatile outbursts toward colleagues.

Industry observers note that wilson calls DC “Babylon on the Potomac,” a biblical moniker he uses to evoke a corrupt place populated by ungodly people. The church has occupied three different locations since it was established, and Wilson has been raising funds to buy a permanent home for it. “We are here for the long haul,” he wrote in a blog post earlier this year. “We believe that it is our responsibility to begin pursuing opportunities to purchase a building near Capitol Hill.” He has also advised on his podcast to not “go to DC and go native” and “[climb] the greasy pole of ambition.” Rather, he mentioned DC “needs an infusion of God-fearing humans.”.

Wilson, who initially agreed to an interview with WIRED and then abruptly canceled with little explanation, hasn’t shied away in past media engagements from touting his newfound clout in government circles. “This is the first time we’ve had connections with as many people in national government as we do now,” Wilson told the Associated Press in 2025, shortly after he came to DC to speak at the opening of his newly introduced church.

Industry observers note that wilson’s rising profile and expansion to DC wouldn’t have been possible without Hegseth, notes Peter Bell, a researcher, theologian, and host of the podcast Sons of Patriarchy, which has been investigating Wilson for years. “Hegseth gave them an in.”.

Industry observers note that “The secretary is a proud member of a church affiliated with the Congregation of Reformed Evangelical Churches, which was founded by Pastor Doug Wilson,” chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told WIRED in response to a request for comment. “The secretary very much appreciates many of Mr. Wilson’s writings and teachings.”.

Parnell subsequently issued a second statement. “Staff at the Department of War have the liberty to practice their faith and attend any church they choose,” he remarked, using the administration’s name for the Defense Department. “It is shameful that WIRED is attempting to smear respected personnel for exercising their religious freedoms.”.

In 2022, well before he was nominated to President Donald Trump’s cabinet, Hegseth moved his family to the Nashville, Tennessee, area to attend a CREC church and enroll his children in an affiliated classical Christian school. After he was narrowly confirmed as secretary of defense last year, Hegseth introduced a regular monthly Pentagon prayer service and brought out his pastor from Tennessee, Brooks Potteiger, to lead the inaugural session. In July, Potteiger officially became the pastor of Christ Church DC.

In a recent development, “I believe this is significant,” Potteiger remarked on a podcast with Wilson and other church elders before his move to DC. “It energizes me … to see these young families, and especially the young Christian men, who are hungry for a soaring biblical view of the lordship of Christ over all things.” (Christ Church DC did not respond to WIRED’s request for an interview with Potteiger.).

As secretary, Hegseth has invoked scripture when talking about the war in Iran, established an office of religious affairs at the Pentagon, and used his position to claim that America is a fundamentally Christian nation. "Our department is, you might say, putting on the full armor of God, because while we wage physical war, we all know the real battle is spiritual," Hegseth said in a speech in late September. "Live your calling. Stand firm. Preach truth. Minister to the flock." He has invited Wilson to speak at Pentagon prayer sessions twice this year. In Wilson’s most recent address to the military, just last week, he told his audience why they are right to want America to become a theocracy and why they are right to want to impose a Christian conservative social order.

Wilson, who describes himself as “paleo-Confederate,” has been a fringe figure for decades and operates within a grab bag of historical Protestant traditions. He’s been seeding his influence through his network of around 160 churches and hundreds of CREC-accredited schools and colleges across the US and internationally, laying the groundwork to take his blueprint for a Christian nationalist society well beyond Idaho. Wilson has made it explicitly clear that he is building toward a new political and social order in America—one that places the church at its center and is ruled by Christian men.

It has been revealed that through various affiliated media outlets, Wilson has said “women need to be pastored, and they need to be pastored by men,” and as recently as 2024 he advocated for the repeal of the 19th Amendment, which gave women the right to vote. This belief system goes back decades: In 1996 he coauthored a booklet describing slavery as a “relationship based upon mutual affection and confidence.” He has said that he doesn’t believe that “a Muslim should be able to hold political office” and called immigration a “deliberately fomented war on the American heritage and unremitting hostility to the culture.”.

Wilson’s reach into the US government now extends beyond Hegseth. Christ Church DC’s new worshipers include Justin Overbaugh, deputy undersecretary of war for intelligence and security at the Defense department; Nate Halverson, chief of staff to the assistant secretary of the Navy for manpower and reserve affairs; C. Scott “Sonny” Duncan, senior counselor to the secretary of the Navy; Stuart Scheller, senior adviser to the US undersecretary of war for personnel and readiness; and Ryan Higgins, senior adviser for religious issues at the Pentagon and one of Hegseth’s key aides.

Overbaugh, a former US Army officer who was working in risk management in Florida until Hegseth nominated him, now deals with highly sensitive military intelligence and counterintelligence. Overbaugh is an attendee of Christ Church DC and is slated to give a seminar in Tampa, Florida, in January titled “Serving Christ in the Pentagon.”.

Halverson graduated from Newly introduced Saint Andrews College, a university in Moscow, Idaho, that Wilson cofounded, in 2006. In October, despite having no military background, Halverson was appointed chief of staff to the assistant secretary of the Navy for manpower and reserve affairs, another senior Pentagon leadership role that is involved with recruiting all Navy and Marine Corps personnel and oversees policies that impact all military and civilian personnel and their families within the Navy. Prior to joining the Pentagon, Halverson spent 15 years working in sales for Verint, a workforce management software firm.

Duncan, who describes himself as “executive servant leader” on his LinkedIn, was recently promoted to senior counselor to the secretary of the Navy, an influential position that allows him to help shape decisions that impact the entirety of US Navy operations. Duncan is a former Marine pilot who retired in 2023 to fly commercial American Airlines planes and work part-time at Chick-fil-A. His decision to retire with the rank of lieutenant colonel was borne out of his objection to the military’s Covid-19 vaccine requirements, which in turn garnered him positive attention in right-wing media circles.

Last year, Hegseth made Duncan a key point of contact for an initiative titled “Reinstating Service Members Negatively Impacted by the Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination Mandate.”.

Sources indicate that scheller, a former Marine who reached the rank of lieutenant colonel, was court-martialed in 2021 after pleading guilty to showing contempt and disrespect for senior military officials over the chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan. Higgins, who has also attended the church, was revealed in a recent CNN investigation to have shared scores of racist and homophobic social media posts targeting immigrants and Muslims. Higgins has also played a key role in shaping Hegseth’s Christian nationalist messaging at the Pentagon, CNN reported.

According to data from 2019, 70 percent of active-duty service members identified as Christian. Mikey Weinstein, a former Air Force officer, attorney, and founder of the Military Religious Freedom Foundation, estimates that around half of those adhere to Christian nationalist ideology. For many of those, he thinks that it’s a case of emulating the ideology that they are seeing from their leaders. Weinstein says that the vast majority of the service members that his organization represents are Christians who feel alarmed by and powerless to push back against Christian nationalism that’s taken hold at all ranks, including at the very top.

Government officials outside of the Pentagon are also involved with Christ Church DC.

Trump administration couple Bethany and Matthew Kozma have attended the church with their children. Bethany Kozma, the director of global affairs at the Department of Health and Human Services—America's top international health diplomat—is known for her positions against abortion and transgender rights. Matthew Kozma is the Department of Homeland Security's undersecretary for intelligence and analysis and oversees all problems related to “counterterrorism, counterproliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and critical infrastructure protection.” Both Bethany and Matthew were contributors to Project 2025.

Sources indicate that the church has also attracted some personnel from the Justice Department, including David Vandenberg, who was hired to the DOJ’s civil rights division last year and was seated last month as an immigration judge. He worked in Newly introduced Mexico and Texas as an assistant US attorney from 2021 to 2024. In Texas, Vandenberg’s colleagues complained of alleged volatile behavior.

Brantley Mayers, a former fellow at the Claremont Institute, a right-wing think tank, works as counsel to the assistant attorney general for the DOJ’s civil division. Mayers was often a spokesperson for the DOJ, defending the Trump administration’s ICE occupation of Minneapolis earlier this year. He was also referred for discipline in June after a federal judge ruled that the DOJ had engaged in “unsettling” practices in its efforts to get a Rhode Island hospital to comply with a subpoena over transgender care. “That is dirty pool, in my opinion, and the Department of Justice have willfully done that in this case,” the judge said at a May 2026 hearing. Mayers represented the DOJ at a hearing for this case.

Sources indicate that another church attendee is Stephen Duggan, chief financial officer at the US International Development Finance Corporation, which invests in private-sector development projects overseas. (Earlier this year, the head of the DFC was questioned by Congressional Democrats about the agency’s investments and their “potential entanglements” with the Trump family.) In the past, Duggan worked as the chief financial officer for Bentkey Ventures, a subscription-based streaming service that offers “anti-woke” children’s content and is owned by the media tech giant The Daily Wire.

Andrew Braun, defense policy adviser for Mike Rounds, a GOP senator from South Dakota and former government relations manager at the conservative think tank The Heritage Foundation, has also attended church services. Paul Lindstrom, who was briefly an offensive lineman for the University of Idaho Vandals football team and worked as an executive assistant in the Office of the President until recently, has attended, as has Samuel Brown, undersecretary for memorial affairs at the Department of Veterans Affairs.

According to recent reports, (WIRED reached out to all the government officials mentioned in this story for comment. None of them replied with the exception of a spokesperson for Bethany Kozma, who initially denied that she’d ever attended the church. When told that WIRED was entirely confident that Kozma had attended at least once, the spokesperson stated she would call back and never did.).

At the church, these officials rub shoulders with members of conservative think tanks, delegates from the CREC network, judicial clerks, venture capitalists, lobbyists, and more.

In a recent development, having like-minded Christians in office is a core part of Wilson’s long-term strategy. “Wilson is explicit concerning his desire to see Christians in office—and only Christians in office—and a church at the foot of the Capitol is the clearest route toward that end,” says Bell.

A core part of Project 2025, the blueprint for Trump’s second term in office, was a proposal to infuse Christian nationalist ideology into all levels of US government. Shortly after taking office, Trump signed an executive order that established a task force to investigate “anti-Christian bias” in government departments, and Christian nationalists were placed in key roles. Across the government, and beyond the Pentagon, this attitude has been replicated: The former secretary of labor began a monthly prayer service months after the creation of a White House Faith Office.

Recent findings suggest that “Doug, in his own words, has always specified a Christian culture comes from the ground up rather than being imposed, and that is crucial here,” said Bell. “Put Christians in office, legislate Christian morality, let that simmer among the populace, and Christian culture eventually emerges.”.

115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The private jets are operated by Qatar Executive - a subsidiary of the Qatar Airways Group, which is one of Fifa's sponsors.
  • Fifa president Gianni Infantino's globetrotting by private jet since his plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup can be revealed.
  • BBC Sport found Infantino has taken 39 private flights - the equivalent of one every three days - and visited 32 different countries since the news emerged on 28 July.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The private jets are operated by Qatar Executive - a subsidiary of the Qatar Airways Group, which is one of Fifa's sponsors.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino's globetrotting by private jet since his plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup can be revealed.

BBC Sport found Infantino has taken 39 private flights - the equivalent of one every three days - and visited 32 different countries since the news emerged on 28 July.

Our research found he travelled more than 102,800 air miles and spent just under nine days in the air in the space of 115 days.

Critics have accused of Infantino of using tools only at his disposal as president to aid his campaign for re-election next March.

They questioned whether his re-election campaign may have partly motivated any promises made or support offered during those visits.

Fifa said Infantino had a "statutory duty to maintain and develop good relations between and among Fifa, the confederations, 211 member associations, political bodies, and international organisations".

However, he visited nearly double the 18 countries he did in the same period in 2025.

The initial Times story that revealed Infantino's World Cup plan led to a wave of criticism around the world.

But, as BBC Sport revealed, many observers feel Infantino is now the favourite to be re-elected in the spring after his rivals struggled to find a candidate to run against him until the last moment.

And it appears Infantino has managed to shore up support around the world, with critics suggesting his globetrotting was a key part of that strategy.

There has also been concern about the environmental impact of his extensive travels.

Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - said Infantino's travelling was "part of his campaign".

He told BBC Sport: "The issue here is that Fifa does not have rules on campaign funding, so the president can claim that he's going there on official business when indirectly he's using that to campaign.

"And anyone else running against him very likely will not have the financial means to compete with that.".

Infantino's position seemed vulnerable after it emerged he had been devising a blueprint to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, in a proposal called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Before FFE was abandoned, Infantino wrote to all 211 member associations saying they would receive $40m (Â£30m) if they backed the plan.

Lars-Christer Olsson - a former chief executive of Uefa - told BBC Sport the "important" question was "what does he promise and what are the conditions, as he already did when he promised cash if the members supported his FFE project?".

BBC Sport gleaned the information about where Infantino had been travelling to, and when, from postings on his social media accounts.

The reasons for his travels include holding meetings with football association presidents, opening pitches, meeting politicians and attending confederation gatherings.

The private jets he used are operated by Qatar Executive (QE) - a subsidiary of the Qatar Airways Group, which is one of Fifa's sponsors.

It has been revealed that BBC Sport used flight-tracking records and the jet registrations of the Qatar Executive fleet to compile a detailed log of Infantino's flights, totalling at least 39 since the start of August. Fifa did not dispute the figure.

It stated "all travel is in line with Fifa's regulations" and there are "rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any Fifa official".

But Fifa declined to comment on how the use of QE flights impacts on the money available from the Qatar Airways sponsorship for the benefit of global football.

The governing body also declined to comment when asked when Infantino had last taken a commercial flight.

Olsson said: "What do these trips cost and who is paying, which are the implications for the total football community?

"Is he provided with transport in his private campaign with the idea of getting something back in return if he is elected? If Fifa is paying for private jets, would it not be better to invest this money in the member associations?".

Maduro said: "That's again a confusion between his role as president of Fifa and his role as candidate to Fifa presidency.".

He mentioned there were no regulations within Fifa on the "use of public money to support their campaign".

"There's no independent authority that controls that, there is no regulation of campaign funding," he mentioned.

Infantino's trips included attending the Caribbean Football Union presidents' meeting and a junior football tournament in the Dominican Republic three weeks after FFE failed.

He then flew to Paris, where he attended the esports World Cup , alongside French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

On his Instagram account, Infantino said he had "pledged Fifa's support" for the Pakistan Football Federation president's development aims when he met him in the US in September.

A few days later, he referenced a "wonderful discussion" with the president of the Latvian Football Federation during a visit to Riga, describing him as "my dear friend".

During a visit to Indonesia in October for the final of the Fifa ASEAN Cup, he met presidents from the football federations of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Philippines, Qatar, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste.

He remarked: "Having your support and shared passion on this momentous occasion means a great deal and together we will continue driving this game forward.".

And during a recent trip to Manila, he performed on stage as part of a quartet called the 'Backache Boys', alongside officials from the Asian Football Confederation, and the football federations of Malaysia and the Philippines.

Gianni Infantino opened a mini-pitch in Anguilla in November.

Gianni Infantino visited the Philippines for the ASEAN Football Federation Ordinary Congress.

Gianni Infantino in Qatar to oversee preparations for the Fifa U17 World Cup.

Based on our log of Infantino's private-jet flights, we calculated he spent 213 hours and 49 minutes in the air, travelling about 102,870 air miles.

For the type of private jet Infantino was using, this would produce an estimated 1,673 tonnes of CO2e emissions.

Industry observers note that that's equivalent to the emissions 252 people would accumulate on average in an entire year, according to European Union data, external. These figures are conservative estimates based on average fuel burn rates.

According to recent reports, fifa has also been criticised for expanding the number of teams at World Cups, and hosting them in multiple countries, thereby increasing the amount of travel. The 2026 World Cup was described as the 'most polluting World Cup ever'.

Freddie Daley, from the Cool Down Sport for Climate Action Network, said Infantino's behaviour was "emblematic of Fifa's approach to environmental sustainability under his leadership: total and utter disregard".

"Despite numerous pledges, Fifa has failed to deliver any significant plan on how it will achieve them and has instead gone backwards," he added.

Maduro said Fifa's support for initiatives on climate action - which included being a signatory of the United Nation's Sports for Climate Action Framework - was "window dressing".

Fifa did not directly respond to a question about its justification for the environmental impact caused by Infantino's extensive travelling.

A spokesperson for Fifa said its objectives were to "improve football constantly and promote it globally".

They added: "The Fifa president has a statutory duty to maintain and develop good relations between and among Fifa, the confederations, 211 member associations, political bodies, and international organisations.

It has been revealed that "To do that, he travels around the world and attends Fifa's tournaments and events. Mr Infantino is elected until 18 March 2027, when the next Fifa presidential election will take place.

"Fifa has put in place rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any Fifa official.

"The Fifa president routinely travels around the world for various duties, together with relevant officials, on business and tournament-related matters and strives to visit member associations of Fifa whenever he can.

"Fifa expenses are published in our annual report, and all travel is in line with Fifa's regulations.

"Fifa's money belongs to the 211 member associations and an increased investment to $6.35bn for the upcoming cycle reinforces our unwavering commitment to further supporting football development and access globally.".

#173709. Industry News: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1179 w)

Industry News: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A remarkable archaeological discovery in southern Saudi Arabia is revealing what life was like 125,000 years ago, when parts of the Arabian Peninsula were covered in lakes, grasslands, and thriving wildlife.
  • The discoveries come from Uruq al-Julaybah, an ancient lakeside site in the Mundafan region.
  • A Lost Green Arabia Filled With Lakes and Wildlife.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A remarkable archaeological discovery in southern Saudi Arabia is revealing what life was like 125,000 years ago, when parts of the Arabian Peninsula were covered in lakes, grasslands, and thriving wildlife. Researchers have uncovered ancient stone tools, fossils of large animals, and rare plant remains that offer an unusually detailed look at how early humans survived in this dramatically different environment.

The discoveries come from Uruq al-Julaybah, an ancient lakeside site in the Mundafan region. Announced by the Saudi Heritage Commission, the findings are the result of a joint investigation involving the Commission, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), and Griffith University. Published in Science, the research brings together specialists in geology, archaeology, botany, and micropaleontology, along with experts from several international institutions. Their work provides vital new evidence about prehistoric human activity, environmental change, and early human presence across the Arabian Peninsula.

A Lost Green Arabia Filled With Lakes and Wildlife.

Sources indicate that today, much of this region is dominated by desert, but the landscape looked very different during the last Interglacial period, around 125,000 years ago. This warm, humid chapter of Arabian history is often called Green Arabia, a time when plentiful water and vegetation supported large animals and human populations.

Recent findings suggest that using satellite-based terrain modeling, scientists reconstructed an enormous ancient lake covering approximately 340 square kilometers. The lake reached depths of up to 29 meters. Evidence from sediments, the surrounding landscape, and the remains of aquatic organisms indicates that it was a relatively stable freshwater environment bordered by open grasslands and vegetation.

It has been revealed that the researchers identified more than 500 plant and animal fossil specimens, including invertebrates, spread across more than 130 locations. Among the animals that once inhabited the area were hippos, extinct long-horned buffaloes, camels, Arabian oryx, gazelles, and ostriches. These discoveries reveal a rich prehistoric ecosystem that bears little resemblance to the dry landscape found there today.

Thousands of Ancient Stone Tools Reveal Human Ingenuity.

Alongside the fossils, archaeologists recovered 5,511 stone tools measuring more than 2 centimeters from the main excavation area. More than 98% were made from flint, and analysis revealed that the people who created them used Levallois techniques, a method of shaping stone to produce carefully prepared flakes.

To better understand how the tools were made and used, researchers conducted systematic surveys using a grid system to document and collect artifacts and fossils. They also applied two dating methods to sand and fossil teeth, used three-dimensional techniques to determine how stone fragments fit together, and examined tool surfaces with microscopic and chemical analyses.

Sources indicate that these investigations uncovered intriguing evidence of how early humans used the plants around them. Residues preserved on stone tools included traces from several types of vegetation, some of which contain toxic compounds. Resin and woody material suggest that certain stone tips were attached to handles or shafts to make hunting weapons.

It has been revealed that other plant residues point to the processing of tubers, bushes, and palm leaves. This suggests that the people living around the lake relied on vegetation for a variety of purposes, from obtaining food to carrying out everyday activities.

Perhaps most surprisingly, the findings raise the possibility that prehistoric hunters incorporated poisonous plant compounds into their hunting technology. Although this interpretation remains tentative, it represents some of the earliest potential evidence of such practices identified in Saudi Arabia. The discoveries also include some of the region's earliest known evidence of palm-related vegetation.

A Rare Glimpse Into Everyday Life 125,000 Years Ago.

Industry observers note that what makes Uruq al-Julaybah especially valuable is the unusual combination of discoveries preserved at one location. The animal fossils, manufactured tools, and plant remains were all recovered from the same dated archaeological setting (animal remains, stone tools, and plant material), allowing scientists to piece together a remarkably complete picture of prehistoric life.

According to recent reports, the shores of ancient Lake Mundafan appear to have provided an ideal gathering place for early humans. Freshwater, animals, vegetation, and materials suitable for making tools were all available in the surrounding landscape.

Evidence suggests that people used this environment for numerous activities, including manufacturing stone tools, preparing hunting equipment, processing animals and plants, and working with plant fibers. Taken together, the discoveries indicate that these early populations were highly adaptable and made sophisticated use of the resources available to them.

"It is very exciting to see how the collaboration of so many different specialists allows to reconstruct this uniquely complete picture of life, behavior and the environment in the distant past," noted Professor Frans van Buchem, KAUST Professor of Geology and co-lead scientist.

Dr. Faisal Al-Jibreen, a Heritage Commission researcher and professor of Paleolithic archaeology who participated in the project, emphasized the importance of the discovery at Lake Mundafan in the Empty Quarter. He described it as a significant archaeological find that helps explain how the ancient environment shaped the lives of humans and animals in southern Saudi Arabia during early prehistory.

Reconstructing a Forgotten Chapter of Human History.

It has been revealed that "This site gives us a rare and richly detailed view of how people lived in a landscape that looks nothing like Arabia today," remarked Professor Chris Clarkson, co-lead scientist and Professor of Archaeology at Griffith University's Australian Research Centre for Human Evolution. "The combination of animal remains, stone tools and plant material in a single, dated context is what makes this discovery so significant.".

By bringing together different kinds of archaeological and environmental evidence, the researchers have reconstructed a period of Arabian history that is difficult to imagine from the region's present-day appearance. Their findings offer crucial clues about how early humans moved across the Arabian Peninsula, developed technology, and adapted their behavior to changing environmental conditions.

It has been revealed that "Saudi Arabia has an exceptional archaeological heritage. Building Heritage Science capabilities in the Kingdom will enable us to turn the smallest traces into the biggest stories," said Professor Laurence Hapiot, co-author and Head of Heritage Research at KAUST.

Recent findings suggest that the investigation reflects an extensive international research effort to better understand the Arabian Peninsula's ancient human and environmental history. The Saudi Heritage Commission supported fieldwork during the 2023 season, helped fund the research, and facilitated scientific activities.

Along with KAUST, Griffith University in Australia, and King Saud University, the project involved international universities and research centers specializing in archaeology, ancient environments, history, and laboratory analysis. This collaboration demonstrates how combining expertise from different scientific fields can uncover extraordinary details about human life thousands of generations in the past.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Debbie Hewitt has been chair at the FA since 2022.

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.

Earlier this month, Fifa mentioned "key documents" on the abandoned blueprint to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".

Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.

Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'â¦ which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".

They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".

The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.

Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.

"As a member association, the FA is entitled to hold the Fifa president accountable for his actions, and as a Fifa Council vice-president, Hewitt should have seen these looks as soon as they were hatched.

"They had the right to demand to see these documents, and should have exercised that right forcefully and publicly, rather than signing a gagging clause that puts Fifa and Infantino back in control.".

However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.

It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.

Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.

Industry observers note that fifa has been approached for comment. 💡 Key Takeaways
